notes.title: The corps strikes!
notes.content: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208062/91edd87cfcc0819d00eb1ad0557473d72a50037f.png"][/img]Hello everyone[/p][p]Today I have good news, because the new 0.7.7 update for the demo game has been released. The main novelty is the new battle admiral of the Imperial Corps![/p][p][/p][h3]What new things does he bring to the game?[/h3][p]This admiral specializes in space infantry and planetary siege warfare. In one of the recent updates, the player has the opportunity to build planetary corps bases for infantry training. Up to this point, they could only provide additional durability to fleets, planets, and stations, as well as serve as labor on defensive platforms. But with the advent of the corps' spaceships, we will begin to reveal their true purpose — boarding and amphibious operations![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208062/e6cc9114c4f29bb34c1a6fa75cae6dc810bccb9f.png"][/img][/p][p]The corps' fleets carry a large number of Imperial infantry with them and are equipped with a large number of boarding capsules. When they engage in battle, they unleash waves of boarding parties on the enemy. For infantrymen, this is a one-way road, but when they get on an enemy ship, they can cause tremendous damage, especially if there are no enemy infantry there.[/p][p][/p][p]In addition, boarding capsules as a weapon completely ignore the shields of the target, without losing their effectiveness.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208062/16908b8fd1f988ce63aa75a4ff8cc96f5ff2f2fc.png"][/img][/p][p]But all this will please the player only until the fleet has enough infantrymen to carry out operations. In protracted battles or with insufficient supplies, corps fleets can lose most of their firepower.[/p][p][/p][p]Another feature of the new fleets are the batteries of artillery guns. There are not as many of them as on other imperial ships, and they cannot boast high damage per minute, but they have significant damage bonuses for the population of planets and stations, which means they can significantly speed up the siege process.[/p][p][/p][p]In addition, the game has undergone a number of improvements and edits in the interface, behavior algorithms and trading. All this can already be tried in the current demo version of the game. I hope you'll like the changes. ^_^[/p]

notes.title: Cosmography
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208062/97e0add2814d6acf35e2942abdbb85ae22456873.png[/img]
Hello everyone

So it's time for the second major update. This time we will talk about interstellar fleet movements and everything related to them. Until now, the space fleets in the game had only one limitation in their interstellar movements — the maximum jump range. This value was substantial and granted considerable freedom to both the player and the opponent. It was all fresh and interesting in its own way, but over time it became clear that there was a downside to such freedom.

Due to the high mobility of enemy fleets, it has become difficult to distinguish between front-line systems and protected internal ones. In some games, players found themselves in a situation where they had to defend almost their entire territory at once, or the enemy attacked from completely unexpected directions 😅

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208062/0855eb27419e2ee91f3995751735f21fd00e60c0.png[/img]

We can also add the inability to accurately predict the route of our own advancing forces and a number of other non-obvious factors. It was necessary to add some order to this chaos 🙄

After much thought, I decided to bring back the mechanics of interstellar communications to the game, which would limit the routes of fleets. I really didn't want to lose this freedom, but due to a combination of factors, I'm sending her under the knife 😑🔪

However, as they say, every cloud has a silver lining. The game has improved control over the gameplay, and the tactical component has grown. Even those systems where there are no resources can be valuable because of their location. The nodal defensive points and systems have been clearly identified, the capture of which will cause damage to enemy logistics. The game has become a little deeper.

All the changes are already available in the demo version of the game, and I hope you will like it!

notes.title: The demo is available!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208062/5f8087a4ee76d8e0c98b097b9289ca1921aa8dd1.jpg[/img]
Hello everyone

Today we are celebrating, because the first demo version of Solar Wave is already available! This is a small, but without a doubt, a very important step towards the release of the game.

What can you try out in the game? 
[list]
[*]A dynamic and lively simulation of a space state with a well-developed economic system
[*]15 types of fleets (including several enemy fleets)
[*]22 different ships for them
[*]a bundle of stations and planets
[*]and 3 missions to test your strategic skills
[/list]
As you can guess, this is not the final version, and many aspects of the game will change by release. The game is developing dynamically, mostly based on your feedback and suggestions. Once again, I want to express my gratitude for your feedback — every day it helps me make Solar Wave better. Thank you for this opportunity!

notes.title: Hostile space and a hell of a lot of changes!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208062/e15126f4f6c3b53ffe9ba7eca8cc2b13b40b8d14.png[/img]
Hi!
The first really big update for the public version of Solar Wave is ready!
Without putting it in the back drawer, a list of changes:

[list]
[*] [b]Hostile Space[/b] - The space around the player is now populated by Terroxenos. The hostile life form has its own stations, planets, and economy. The development of territories will no longer be an easy walk.

[*] [b]Enemy attacks[/b] - the logic of attacking enemy fleets has changed, they can still invade directly into the player's territory, but in most cases they will raid from their possessions.

[*] [b]Defensive stations[/b] - The addition of opponents on the map led to the formation of a front line and the division into rear and peripheral systems. In this regard, the first defensive stations have been added to the game, which can strengthen defenses in key positions.

[*] [b]Imperial Troops [/b] are the first alternative population type introduced in the game. Troops can be trained on your planets in a special structure. They serve on defensive platforms and in most imperial fleets. Troops are not used in amphibious operations [b]yet[/b], but it can significantly reduce incoming damage.

[*] [b]Interface improvements[/b] - numerous UI improvements, now it should be a little easier to understand what is happening in the game.

[*] [b]As well as a bunch of other minor edits.[/b]
[/list]
I hope you enjoy the updates in the game, and I'm also looking forward to your feedback and comments!

notes.title: The playtest has been launched!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=tUwAQM_UiGs;full][/previewyoutube]
Hello everyone!
Today I have good news - the first open Solar Wave playtest has already started! Anyone can participate.

What awaits us all? 13 types of fleets (including several enemy ones), 20 different ships for them, a pack of stations and planets, a tricky economic system and 3 missions to play with it all.
This playtest will focus on simulating the state and the work of the economy, so you won't have to go on aggressive campaigns yet. But don't expect your opponents to leave you alone — it's going to be very hot at times!

Be sure to play the training mission "The Beginning of the Invasion" - it will help you figure out how everything works here. I hope you enjoy it. 😊

PS: When closing, the game will prompt you to leave a small feedback. I would be extremely grateful if you would do this. This will help me adjust the direction of the game's development and make it better. Thank you in advance! 😌

notes.title: Playtest is coming!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208062/6c5901b2962a5b90e834a343af805e97a24ab720.jpg[/img]
Hello everyone!

I have some good news! Until now, the only way to experience the role of the imperial governor was to visit one of the showcases featuring Solar Wave or to end up in my caring hands during closed tests. 🤗

But! Those times are coming to an end, and everyone will have the chance to try the game! Registration for the open playtest has already started on the game's page. 🎉
We're aiming for January, so make sure to register so you don't miss out! After all, "The Invasion must take place!" (c)

notes.title: Solar Wave on Steam!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45208062/0d2fff5058af660937f00211a46cc9d734acda57.jpg[/img]
Well, the day has finally arrived! Solar Wave on Steam!

Hi! Let me introduce myself. My name is Dmitry and I am the developer of the Solar Wave game. This is a very exciting day for me, as after a year of hard work, the game is finally ready to be shown to you.
Of course, there is still a lot of work ahead - spaceships, game mechanics, a variety of treacherous enemies, new battle modes - all this will not add itself to the game. But step by step, I'll get there, and soon we'll reach the moment when the game will be released.

So welcome aboard, Governor, and let's see where this journey takes us!
